newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat to up into jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat to up into jobs data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended Thursday's quiet session flat to a touch higher ahead of Friday's key May employment report.

"(Muni) futures closed up six ticks, but the cash market didn't really move that much," one trader said. "Cash has run up pretty good, and its been pretty rich. The contract seems to keep marching forward though. The MOB seems to pick up 1/8 to 1/4 everyday."
Economists polled by Reuters expect non-farm payrolls to show a 219,000 increase. If a hostile number prints, the trader said munis are likely to outperform U.S. Treasuries on the way down.
"They might actually lag on the upside because they have been outperforming," he said.
The trader expects municipals to continue to outperform governments for the near term at least.

"Demand and supply seem to be reasonably in balance, and you know you are going into a time of year where you get a decent amount of interest payments made and bond calls," he said. "Whether people will roll that money back into the market is another question, but sometimes dealers will run the market up in anticipation of selling bonds to customers."
Back in Thursday's muni cash market, an analyst said high-grade issues ended unchanged to "up a touch selectively."
Dollar bonds ended unchanged with a slight bias upward. Secondary activity was light to moderate.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was flat at 96-24/32 to yield 6.88 percent in late New York trade. In debt futures, the September municipal contract closed up 6/32 at 116-8/32. The September T-bond contract closed down 1/32 at 110. The MOB spread was 200 ticks.
Looking ahead to next week, $3.5 billion of fresh municipal debt is expected. Competitive sales are expected to total $1.6 billion, while negotiated deals are expected to hit $1.9 billion.

Topping the negotiated list is a $540 million Puerto Rico Public Buildings Authority via Smith Barney Inc. The largest competitive deal is a $225 million Virginia Housing Development Authority offering set for Tuesday.
Reuters said Thursday it calculated its 30-day visible supply of upcoming municipal bond sales at $5.020 billion, up $501 million from Wednesday.
